format:

    nav-buttons: []
    include-after-body:
      text: |
        <script>
        // Plotly measures text (legends, value labels) while a dashboard card is still hidden and
        // caches the zero widths per font. Once a chart is visible, a tiny font-name change forces a
        // fresh measurement -- on load and whenever a dashboard page or card tab is shown.
        function dvRedraw() {
          document.querySelectorAll('.js-plotly-plot').forEach(function (el) {
            if (el.clientWidth > 0 && el.offsetParent !== null && !el.dataset.dvDone) {
              el.dataset.dvDone = '1';
              Plotly.relayout(el, {'font.family': el._fullLayout.font.family + ', Arial'});
            }
          });
        }
        window.addEventListener('load', function () { setTimeout(dvRedraw, 200); });
        document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', function () { setTimeout(dvRedraw, 50); });
        </script>
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false

```{python}
#| include: false
# Reads the pipeline's own outputs -- nothing is recomputed or looked up here.
# Folder: DV_OUT_DIR (same variable as run_pipeline.py), else ../output.
# Every chart card has a "Data" tab: the rows behind the chart + CSV downloads (counts and rows).
import os, re, urllib.parse
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown, HTML

OUT = os.environ.get("DV_OUT_DIR") or os.path.join("..", "output")
S = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "summary.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
D = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "per_dataset.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")

# ---- verdict categories: fixed order + fixed colours (colour follows the category, never its rank)
# Shared own data is split by access: deposited with restricted access still counts as shared
# ("as open as possible, as closed as necessary"), but is never shown as open. Same blue hue, lighter.
SHARED, SH_RESTR, SH_UNK = ("shared own data (open)", "shared own data (restricted access)",
                            "shared own data (access unknown)")
REGONLY, REUSE, DECL, NONE = ("no data in paper; dataset linked via DataCite", "reuses data only",
                              "declared, unverifiable", "no data found")
NOGEN  = "no data generated (paper says so)"   # nodata.py: the paper's own words
ONREQ  = "own data on request only (not shared)"  # nodata.on_request: data exist, not deposited
ORDER  = [SHARED, SH_RESTR, SH_UNK, ONREQ, REGONLY, REUSE, DECL, NOGEN, NONE]
LABEL  = {SHARED: "Shares own data: open", SH_RESTR: "Shares own data: restricted access",
          SH_UNK: "Shares own data: access unknown", ONREQ: "Own data on request only (not shared)", REGONLY: "DataCite link only (not counted)",
          REUSE: "Reuses data only", DECL: "Declared, not verifiable",
          NOGEN: "No data generated (paper says so)", NONE: "No data found (not shared, or no data)"}
# the two "no data" categories share the gray family; lighter = the paper explains it has none
COLOR  = {SHARED: "#2a78d6", SH_RESTR: "#86b6ef", SH_UNK: "#cde2fb", ONREQ: "#6250d6", REGONLY: "#eb6834", REUSE: "#1baf7a",
          DECL: "#eda100", NOGEN: "#dedcd3", NONE: "#b4b2a8"}
INK, INK2, GRID, SURF = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e8e7e3", "#fcfcfb"

def style(fig, h=None):
    fig.update_layout(template="plotly_white", font=dict(family="'Source Sans Pro', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif", size=13, color=INK2),
                      paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", barcornerradius=4,
                      margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=8, b=8), height=h, hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color=INK),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.15, x=0, title=None, traceorder="normal"))
    fig.update_xaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False, linecolor=GRID)
    fig.update_yaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False, linecolor=GRID)
    return fig

def pct(a, b): return f"{100 * a / b:.0f}%" if b else "–"

def _csv_link(df, label, filename):
    """A download button with the CSV inlined as a data: URI (BOM so Excel reads UTF-8)."""
    uri = "data:text/csv;charset=utf-8," + urllib.parse.quote("﻿" + df.to_csv(index=False))
    return (f'<a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" style="display:inline-block !important;width:auto !important;flex:0 0 auto !important" '
            f'download="{filename}" href="{uri}">{label}</a>')

def data_tab(rows, name, counts=None):
    """Data tab of a chart card: download buttons + the rows behind the chart, as a table.
    The table scrolls in its own box, so the dashboard's sticky table header can't cover the buttons."""
    btns = _csv_link(rows, f"Download rows ({len(rows)}) as CSV", f"{name}_rows.csv")
    if counts is not None:
        btns = _csv_link(counts, "Download counts (as in the chart) as CSV", f"{name}_counts.csv") + btns
    table = rows.to_html(index=False, border=0, escape=True, classes="table table-sm table-striped small")
    return HTML('<div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;min-height:0">'
                f'<div style="display:flex !important;flex-direction:row !important;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;'
                f'padding-bottom:8px;flex:none !important">{btns}</div>'
                f'<div style="flex:1;min-height:0;overflow:auto">{table}</div></div>')

# ---- paper level
S["verdict"] = pd.Categorical(S["data_verdict"], ORDER, ordered=True)
S["key"] = S["paper"].str.replace(r"\.[^.]+$", "", regex=True).str.lower()
NAME = dict(zip(S.key, S.paper))                    # per_dataset's paper key -> file name
N = len(S)
n_shared = int(S.data_verdict.str.startswith("shared own data").sum())   # open + restricted access
n_open   = int((S.data_verdict == SHARED).sum())
n_req    = int((S.on_request_signal != "").sum())                         # "available on request"

AREAS = {"1": "Natural sciences", "2": "Engineering & technology", "3": "Medical & health sciences",
         "4": "Agricultural & veterinary sciences", "5": "Social sciences", "6": "Humanities & the arts"}
def areas(row):
    """SSIF area = first digit of each Swepub code. A paper with codes in two areas counts in both."""
    if row.field_source.startswith("swepub"):
        return sorted({AREAS.get(c[0], "Other") for c in re.findall(r"(?:^|; )(\d{1,5})\b", row.field)})
    # 'swepub (SSIF)' and 'swepub classify (SSIF, automatic)' both carry SSIF codes (matched above).
    # OpenAlex topics (ASJC) don't map 1:1 onto SSIF, so they are not forced into an SSIF area here.
    return ["No SSIF field"]
S["areas"] = S.apply(areas, axis=1)

# ---- dataset level: datasets the papers share as their own (counted)
D["counted"] = (D.status == "confirmed") & (D.provenance == "own")
OWN = D[D.counted].merge(S[["key", "year"]], left_on="paper", right_on="key", how="left")
OWN["paper"] = OWN.paper.map(lambda k: NAME.get(k, k))
```

## Row {height=440px}

### Column {.tabset}

```{python}
#| title: "Restricted access: own datasets vs their own repositories, by research field"
# From field_norm.py (optional): each own DataCite dataset next to the other datasets in ITS repository,
# in the SSIF area of the citing paper (or the whole repository when the repository sets no subjects or
# the area is small). Expected = mean of those references over the datasets. Same rules on both sides.
FN_PATH = os.path.join(OUT, "field_norm_datasets.csv")
HAVE_NORM = os.path.exists(FN_PATH)
if HAVE_NORM:
    FD = pd.read_csv(FN_PATH, encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype={"ssif_area": str})
    FD["paper"] = FD.paper.map(lambda k: NAME.get(k, k))
    FC = FD[FD.reference.notna()].copy()                                   # DataCite datasets only
    FC["area_label"] = FC.ssif_area.map(AREAS).fillna("No SSIF field")
    ALL_OWN = "All own datasets"
    groups = [ALL_OWN] + [a for a in AREAS.values() if a in set(FC.area_label)]
    def refs_text(g):
        c = g.groupby(["repository", "reference"]).size()
        return "<br>".join(f"{r} ({how}): {n}" for (r, how), n in c.items())
    o, e = dict(y=[], text=[], customdata=[]), dict(y=[], text=[], customdata=[])
    for gname in groups:
        if gname == ALL_OWN:          # one row per dataset: average its references over its areas
            g = FC.groupby("identifier").agg(restricted=("restricted", "first"),
                                             ref_share_restricted=("ref_share_restricted", "mean"),
                                             repository=("repository", "first"),
                                             reference=("reference", "first")).reset_index()
        else:
            g = FC[FC.area_label == gname]
        k, n = int(g.restricted.sum()), len(g)
        o["y"].append(100 * k / n); o["text"].append(f"{k}/{n}")
        o["customdata"].append(f"{k} of {n} own dataset(s)")
        ev = 100 * g.ref_share_restricted.mean()
        e["y"].append(ev); e["text"].append(f"{ev:.0f}%")
        e["customdata"].append("references used (datasets):<br>" + refs_text(g))
    NAMES = ["Own datasets in these papers", "Expected from their repositories"]
    fig = go.Figure([go.Bar(x=groups, y=t["y"], text=t["text"], customdata=t["customdata"], name=nm,
                            marker_color=c, textposition="outside", textfont=dict(color=INK2, size=11),
                            cliponaxis=False,
                            hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>" + nm + ": %{y:.0f}%<br>%{customdata}<extra></extra>")
                     for t, nm, c in zip([o, e], NAMES, [COLOR[SHARED], "#8d8b84"])])
    _ = fig.update_layout(barmode="group", bargap=0.3, bargroupgap=0.08)
    _ = style(fig).update_layout(yaxis=dict(ticksuffix="%", range=[0, 100],
                                            title=dict(text="% of datasets with restricted access")))
    display(fig)
else:
    display(Markdown("No reference yet. Run `python field_norm.py` after the pipeline (asks DataCite, a "
                     "few minutes) to write `field_norm.csv` and `field_norm_datasets.csv`, then render again."))
```

### Column

```{python}
#| title: "About the repository comparison"
Markdown("""
Each own dataset is compared with **the other datasets in its own repository**, in the SSIF area of
the paper that cites it. When the repository sets no field subjects, or has fewer than 20 datasets in
that area, the whole repository is the reference (hover to see which). *Expected* = the average of
those references, so the grey bar is what these repositories usually look like for this mix of
datasets.

Same rule on both sides, as in the rest of the dashboard: a deposited dataset has **restricted
access** when its DataCite access right says restricted, closed or embargoed; otherwise it is
**open** (the rest of each bar up to 100 %). Versions of one dataset count once.

**Why not all of DataCite?** Only a few repositories put field subjects on datasets (figshare, the
specimen registry DiSSCo), so an all-of-DataCite figure mostly describes them. Within one repository,
practice is comparable: SND, for instance, has many restricted datasets (personal data), Zenodo few.

**Limits:** it is about *datasets*, not the share of *papers* that share data. Accessions (ENA …)
are not in DataCite and not compared. With few own datasets per area, the bars show *k/n*.

Refresh with `python field_norm.py` (date in the Data tab, column `fetched`).
""")
```

## Row {height=330px}

```{python}
#| title: "How to read this"
Markdown(f"""
**Shares own data** = the paper itself tells the reader where the authors' own data is, and the
identifier resolves to a dataset. It is split by access: **open**, or **restricted access**
(deposited with a DOI and metadata, but access on conditions, e.g. personal data; a paper with some
open and some restricted datasets is shown as restricted). Restricted data count as shared ("as open
as possible, as closed as necessary"); data "available on request" without a deposit do not.
**DataCite link only** = a repository's metadata points to the
paper, but the paper does not cite the dataset; it is shown but *not counted* as sharing.

**Field**: the SSIF area is the first digit of the paper's SSIF codes. They come from the paper's
Swepub record, or, for papers not in Swepub, from Swepub's automatic classifier run on the title and
abstract (`field_source` = *swepub classify*; on this corpus it agreed with the manual Swepub area
whenever it made a suggestion). A paper with codes in two areas counts in both, so the field bars can
add up to more than {N}. *No SSIF field* = neither worked (e.g. no DOI, or no abstract). Colours in the field chart follow the legend of the year chart.

**Results** count *papers*, so papers without data stay in the picture. *No data generated* =
the paper itself says it has no data of its own ("no new data were generated", "data sharing not
applicable"; pattern search, see `no_data_signal`).
*Own data on request only* = the paper shares no data but says its data are available from the
authors on request: the data exist but are not deposited, so they don't count as shared. The KPI
counts every paper with such a sentence, also papers that deposit some of their data.
*No data found* = everything else without data: not shared, or no data, which the tool can't tell apart.

**Repository**: the repository that registered the DOI in DataCite (e.g. SND, Chalmers DORIS,
SciLifeLab), not the `publisher` field, which names the responsible institution (hover to see it).
Accessions (ENA, PRIDE …) show the archive.

**Data tab** on each chart: the rows behind it, with CSV downloads of the counts and of the rows.
Source: `{os.path.abspath(OUT)}`. Every number here comes from `summary.csv` / `per_dataset.csv`
(and `field_norm.csv` for the DataCite comparison).
""")
```


# Tool check {scrolling="true"}

```{python}
#| include: false
# Everything the tool itself is unsure about, as one to-do list: (paper, id, issue, what to do).
# Sources: per_dataset.csv, merged_output.csv (dv_disagreement), selfcheck.csv (answer key).
M = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "merged_output.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
C = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "selfcheck.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
G_ID, G_TOOLS, G_PAPER = "Broken or missing ids", "DFP and DFP-Verify differ", "Paper metadata"
rows = []
def add(group, issue, paper, ident, todo): rows.append(dict(group=group, issue=issue, paper=paper, identifier=ident, todo=todo))

cause = dict(zip(C.identifier, C.broken_id_cause))
for _, r in D[D.registry.str.startswith("repaired")].iterrows():
    written = r.registry[len("repaired (text had "):-1]
    cs = cause.get(r.identifier, "")
    if cs == "as-printed":
        add(G_ID, "Wrong id printed in the paper", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Paper prints {written}. Registered DOI used; worth reporting to authors / publisher")
    elif cs == "pdf-extraction":
        add(G_ID, "Id broken by PDF text extraction", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Text had {written}; the PDF itself is right. Registered DOI used, nothing to fix in the paper")
    else:
        add(G_ID, "Id repaired, cause not checked", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Text had {written}. Set DV_PDF_DIR to check the PDF")
for _, r in D[D.status == "likely-broken-link"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Declared link does not resolve", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
        "Check by hand: typo, private/review link, or removed record")
for _, r in D[D.status == "likely-no-doi"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Declared without a resolvable id", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
        "Data statement points to a site, not a record; check by hand")
for _, r in C[C.result.str.startswith("not found")].iterrows():
    add(G_TOOLS, "Known dataset not found in the text", r.paper, r.identifier,
        f"DataCite links it and the paper cites it as {r.cited_as}; neither text detector picked it up")

for _, r in M[M.dv_disagreement != ""].iterrows():
    for part in r.dv_disagreement.split("; "):
        if part.startswith("detect:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Not in DFP output, found by the other sources", r.file, r.identifier,
                "Found by " + " + ".join({"llm": "DFP", "regex": "pattern search", "datacite": "DataCite",
                                          "text": "web link in text"}.get(t, t)
                                         for t in part.split("(found by ")[-1].rstrip(")").split("+")))
        elif part.startswith("isdata:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "DFP lists it as data, registry says not data", r.file, r.identifier,
                "Registry type: " + (r.dv_verdict.split("(")[-1].rstrip(")") or "?") + ". Usually a cited article; check if wanted")
        elif part.startswith("prov:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Own vs reused differs", r.file, r.identifier, part[len("prov: "):])
        elif part.startswith("open:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Open vs restricted differs", r.file, r.identifier, part[len("open: "):])

pdoi = M.groupby("file").agg(check=("dv_paper_doi_check", "first"), given=("paper_doi", "first"), doi=("dv_paper_doi", "first"))
for f, r in pdoi.iterrows():
    if r.check == "corrected":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI corrected by title check", f, r.doi, f"Given: {r.given or 'none'}. Check which is right")
    elif r.check == "found":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI found by title check", f, r.doi, "No DOI was given")
    elif r.check == "unconfirmed":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI not confirmed", f, r.given, "No DataCite lookup or field for this paper; check the DOI")
for p, g in D[D.status == "datacite-only"].groupby("paper"):
    add(G_PAPER, "DataCite links datasets the paper doesn't cite", NAME.get(p, p), f"{len(g)} dataset(s)",
        "Not counted. Check the published version, or the dataset's metadata")
# the paper says it has no data of its own, but the tool found own or declared data in it
for _, r in S[(S.no_data_signal != "") & (S.data_verdict.str.startswith("shared own data")
                                          | (S.data_verdict == DECL))].iterrows():
    add(G_PAPER, "Paper says it has no data, yet cites own data", r.paper, r.no_data_signal[:90],
        "Read the data statement: is the cited dataset the authors' own?")

Q = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["group", "issue", "paper", "identifier", "todo"])
GCOL = {G_ID: COLOR[SHARED], G_TOOLS: COLOR[REGONLY], G_PAPER: COLOR[REUSE]}
```

## Row {height=160px}

```{python}
#| title: "Who found each dataset (in the text, or only via DataCite)"
def finder(src):
    s = set(src.split("+"))
    if "llm" in s and "regex" in s: return "Both text searches (DFP + pattern search)"
    if "llm" in s:                  return "DFP only"
    if "regex" in s:                return "Pattern search only"
    if "text" in s:                 return "Found via DataCite; paper gives a web link, not the DOI"
    return "Only in DataCite; paper doesn't mention it (not counted)"
FIND = ["Both text searches (DFP + pattern search)", "DFP only", "Pattern search only",
        "Found via DataCite; paper gives a web link, not the DOI", "Only in DataCite; paper doesn't mention it (not counted)"]
R = D[D.status.isin(["confirmed", "datacite-only"]) | D.status.str.startswith("likely")].copy()
R["finder"] = R.source.map(finder)
R["kind2"] = R.status.map(lambda s: "Verified dataset" if s == "confirmed" else
                          ("DataCite link only (not counted)" if s == "datacite-only" else "Declared, not verifiable"))
ft = R.groupby(["finder", "kind2"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(FIND[::-1]).fillna(0).astype(int)
fig = go.Figure()
for k, col in [("Verified dataset", COLOR[SHARED]), ("DataCite link only (not counted)", COLOR[REGONLY]),
               ("Declared, not verifiable", COLOR[DECL])]:
    if k in ft and ft[k].sum():
        _ = fig.add_bar(y=ft.index, x=ft[k], orientation="h", name=f"{k} ({int(ft[k].sum())})",
                        marker=dict(color=col, line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x}<extra>" + k + "</extra>")
_ = style(fig).update_layout(barmode="stack", legend=dict(y=-0.2))
fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Data"
data_tab(R.assign(paper=R.paper.map(lambda k: NAME.get(k, k)))
          [["paper", "identifier", "finder", "kind2", "source", "repository"]]
          .rename(columns={"finder": "found_by", "kind2": "result", "source": "source_code"})
          .sort_values(["found_by", "paper"]), "who_found_what",
         counts=ft.iloc[::-1].rename_axis("found_by").reset_index())
```

```{python}
#| title: "How the self-check works"
# selfcheck.csv: datasets DataCite links to a paper AND the paper cites -> a free answer key
n_dfp = int(C.found_by.str.contains("DFP").sum())
n_pat = int(C.found_by.str.contains("regex").sum())
WHY = {"landing page": "the paper gives the dataset's web page, not its DOI",
       "doi (malformed)": "the dataset link in the text is broken"}
missed = [f"{NAME.get(str(r.paper).rsplit('.', 1)[0].lower(), r.paper)} ({WHY.get(r.cited_as, r.cited_as)})"
          for r in C[~C.result.str.startswith("found")].itertuples()]
Markdown(f"""
Normally we can't know which datasets a paper *should* have. One exception: the dataset's record in
DataCite says it belongs to the paper, **and** the paper cites it. Then the right answer is certain,
so these datasets work as a small test for the two text searches.

**This run:** {len(C)} such datasets. Found {n_found}: DFP {n_dfp}, pattern search {n_pat}.
{"Missed: " + "; ".join(missed) + "." if missed else "None missed."}

**Limits:** only repositories that record the link back to the paper take part (mostly SND and
Chalmers DORIS, rarely Zenodo). It shows how often the searches *miss* data, not how often they
report something that isn't data.
""")
```

```{python}
#| title: "How to read this"
Markdown("""
Datasets are found in three ways. **DFP** is the AI detector that reads the paper. **Pattern search**
is DFP-Verify's own rule-based search of the same text, for anything shaped like a DOI or an archive
accession number (e.g. `PRJEB84056`). **DataCite** works the other way round: a repository's metadata
says the dataset belongs to the paper. If the paper then turns out to cite it by web link, it counts;
if the paper doesn't mention it at all, it is listed but not counted. The self-check uses those
DataCite links as an answer key for the two text searches.
""")
```
